A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Task Tokens study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original appendices A-D correspond to v2 appendices B, C, E, and F, allowing retained material to be distinguished from additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on five humanoid-control tasks, convergence and robustness results, architectural ablations, and a 96-participant human study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a fine-tuning comparison to the robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions train a task encoder with PPO to supply a 512-dimensional token to frozen MaskedMimic, optionally alongside existing prompting modalities. v2's encoder details and finite-state-machine explanation document the existing procedure; proximity-based switching between orientation and kicking prompts already appears in v1 Section 4.4.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Reach, Direction, Steering, Strike, and Long Jump in Isaac Gym with the SMPL humanoid, including the same friction/gravity perturbations and prompting scenarios. v2 newly describes AMP's locomotion-focused training corpus without establishing a change in the data used.

E2.justification: v2 adds MaskedMimic Fine-Tune to both robustness panels in Figure 4, where it was absent in v1. Comparator membership in the main performance tables, convergence plot, human study, and tabulated ablations remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, parallel-environment counts, network widths, task success criteria, checkpoint selection, and human-study design remain unchanged. The added normalization, AMP data, and phase-switching descriptions disclose settings rather than establish revised experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 4 extends the existing robustness analysis to examine full fine-tuning under friction and gravity changes. Appendix A also newly reports unquantified preliminary checks suggesting more complex encoders were unnecessary. The numerical ablations in Tables 3-4 and existing prompting examples are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 adds uncertainty values to human-study percentages, for example changing 95.45% to 95% ± 2%. v2 also identifies plot shading as one standard deviation across five training seeds and explains the zero-shot baseline's omitted variance. The seed count is unchanged, and the human-study uncertainty estimation procedure is not clearly explained.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds fine-tuning results showing a sharper performance decline under increased gravity. v2 also newly reports qualitative findings about lost multimodal prompting after fine-tuning and preliminary encoder-complexity checks. Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain identical numbers, Figure 3 retains its curves, and Table 2's central percentages differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, reinforcement-learning objective, token dimensions, and human-study win-rate definition are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs; the added finite-state-machine description explains an existing control sequence without introducing new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The central claims remain parameter-efficient adaptation through a frozen BFM, hybrid prompting, rapid convergence, robustness, and retained motion quality. v2 foregrounds the existing 125-fold parameter and sixfold convergence comparisons in its abstract and contribution list rather than introducing new central claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands the brief limitations into Section 5, addressing validation on only MaskedMimic, expert-designed rewards and observations, real-robot applicability, and scaling separate encoders to multitask learning. Sections 4.2-4.4 also add explanations involving fine-tuning, overfitting, forgetting, and PULSE's stronger motion prior, substantially broadening interpretation and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: ReLU activations and running input normalization, A100/V100 hardware and 1-2 GPU-days per seed, hyperparameter sources, AMP's motion-data selection, and deterministic prompt switching. It also adds a code-access link. These are documentation additions; the linked resource was not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al., Houlsby et al., and Li and Liang to position Task Tokens relative to parameter-efficient NLP adaptation, plus Goodfellow et al. for catastrophic forgetting. The existing humanoid-control and BFM related-work coverage remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the abstract, introductory motivation, results interpretation, and summary, adds an explicit contribution list and dedicated limitations section, and expands the appendix organization. This changes the explanatory narrative substantially despite retaining the core method and most experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes title, author, and heading formatting, relocates retained displays, revises Figure 1, expands Figure 4's curves and legend, and adds the Figure 8 state diagram. Table 2 incorporates uncertainty, and Figure 3 removes the misleading percent sign from its fractional success-rate axis without changing the plotted results.

improvement.justification: Adding full fine-tuning to Figure 4 strengthens assessment of the frozen-model robustness argument, while expanded implementation information and specific limitations improve transparency. The principal experiments and findings remain stable. Unexplained human-study uncertainty estimates and speculative overfitting explanations limit the gains, supporting a modest overall improvement.
